- Audit/check timestamp:
- Account ID and source rows/workspace aliases:
- Locked-primary or reserve status:
- Deeper integration use: pass/fail + evidence timestamp:
- Usage-ceiling crossing: pass/fail + event timestamp:
- Qualifying human-admin activity: pass/fail + event timestamp:
- Current admin status and deactivation check: pass/fail + checked timestamp:
- Customer Success current state: clear/suppressed/unknown + evidence timestamp:
- Conflict or staleness check:
- Final eligibility decision: PASS / FAIL (fail closed)
- Reason and corrective action:
- Exposure, handoff, and outcome fields (record separately; do not infer from eligibility):

Validated fixture cases
The cases below preserve the validated historical fixture decisions. “PASS” means eligible for the bounded pilot at the relevant check; “FAIL” means excluded or suppressed under the fail-closed rule.

Fixture A — PASS
Expected decision: PASS / eligible.
Validated reason: The rerun correctly admitted A; it satisfied the required eligibility checks, including the three readiness signals, qualifying current human-admin evidence, and a clear Customer Success adoption-and-renewal state.
Audit action: Admit only for an approved account-level exposure if the same checks are fresh and valid at the actual exposure check.

Audit action: Exclude; do not compensate for the missing/failing human signal with service-token activity.

Audit action: Exclude; do not carry forward an older human-activity signal.

Audit action: Suppress until the current Customer Success state is explicitly clear and freshly verified.

Fixture E — FAIL

Audit action: Exclude; missing readiness signals cannot be substituted or inferred.

Fixture F — PASS

The June 28 rerun incorrectly marked G eligible because it did not perform this current-status join.

Historical handling notes
- The June 28 fixture rerun correctly admitted A and F and excluded B, C, D, and E; G was the identified false pass and must be recorded as FAIL under the corrected current-status control.
- Historical held records are not silently converted into passes or failures: when required source data was stale pending refresh, they were held pending the corrected extract and excluded from finalized pass-rate conclusions until reevaluated.

arguments.title: Postmortem — EXP-2023-02-pricing-page
arguments.body:
EXP-2023-02-pricing-page
Postmortem: pricing-page revision

Date / status
- Test window: launched 2023-03-07 at 50%; powered read after two weeks; rolled back 2023-03-20, with the flag confirmed at 0% on 2023-03-22.
- PostHog flag: pricing_page_2023q2_rev.
- Final flag state: rollout 0%, status rolled_back. Preserve the historical exposure and holdout data; do not read the current 0% state as an absence of historical treatment assignment.
- Metric of record: signup-to-paid conversion, primarily for self-serve Starter and Growth traffic.

Hypothesis
A clearer pricing-page package—simplified layout, explicit value-per-seat framing, and less visual clutter—would lift started checkouts per pricing-page visitor and, more importantly, signup-to-paid conversion for self-serve Starter and Growth users. The original target was at least +1.5 percentage points on Starter/Growth signup-to-paid conversion.

Design
Population and assignment
- Eligible audience: self-serve Starter and Growth users only. Enterprise and other non-target plans were excluded.
- Treatment: pricing page revision rendered when pricing_page_2023q2_rev resolved to treatment.
- Control / holdout: the same eligible audience with the flag resolving to the unchanged pricing page.
- Allocation: 50% treatment / 50% holdout during the live window.
- Assignment must be persistent at the account/user level for the read; users must not move arms between pageviews.
- Primary analysis cohort: eligible users with a pricing-page exposure during the live window, analyzed by assigned arm; exclude pre-exposure conversions and post-rollback exposures from the primary read.

Exact PostHog exposure rule
The historical launch rule was: Starter + Growth only, with a 50% rollout on pricing_page_2023q2_rev. In plain terms, include only self-serve accounts whose plan/tier is Starter or Growth, then randomly assign 50% to the revision and retain the other 50% as holdout. Exclude all other plans and any users/accounts outside the self-serve audience. The available flag record stores the audience as “Starter + Growth only”; the underlying PostHog property key/value expression is not present in the experiment registry, so it is not reproduced here as an invented field name.

Timing and rollback
- Launch: 2023-03-07.
- Live read: 50% traffic for approximately two weeks.
- Decision: powered two-week read was complete by 2023-03-20; rollback was executed rather than extending the test.
- Rollback: set pricing_page_2023q2_rev to 0%; preserve exposure/holdout assignments and all events for analysis. The flag was confirmed off on 2023-03-22.

Instrumentation
The instrumentation plan was reviewed and approved by Daniela. The analysis must retain the complete event trail, with one stable user/account identifier and the experiment assignment attached or joinable on every downstream event.

Required event contract
1. Pricing-page pageview
   - Emit once per actual pricing-page view, with event timestamp, stable user/account ID, session ID, page/version, plan/tier, self-serve eligibility, and whether the rendered page was control or treatment.
   - Dedupe retries and client replays; retain raw events and the deduplication key.

2. Flag exposure
   - Emit when pricing_page_2023q2_rev is evaluated for an eligible user/account and the variant is actually available to render—not merely when the flag definition is fetched.
   - Record flag key exactly as pricing_page_2023q2_rev, resolved variant, rollout/assignment decision, stable assignment ID, eligibility inputs, timestamp, and source (client/server).
   - Count exposure only once per stable assignment for primary attribution; retain repeated evaluations separately for QA.
   - A pageview without a corresponding exposure is an instrumentation failure to investigate, not an implicit control observation.

3. Signup start
   - Emit when a visitor submits or begins the signup flow from the pricing page, not on CTA impression alone.
   - Record source page/version, variant, stable user/account ID where available, session ID, plan selected, and timestamp.
   - Preserve the relationship to the preceding pricing-page exposure/pageview.

4. Checkout start
   - Emit when the checkout flow is actually initialized, not when a pricing CTA is clicked without checkout creation.
   - Record checkout/session ID, stable user/account ID, selected plan, currency/amount if available, source page/version, variant, and timestamp.
   - Enforce one canonical checkout-start event per checkout attempt; retries must be linked rather than counted as new starts.

5. Paid conversion
   - Emit or join from the authoritative payment/subscription record when the first eligible payment succeeds, not on checkout completion or a merely created subscription.
   - Record stable user/account ID, subscription/invoice/payment ID, plan/tier, amount/currency, conversion timestamp, source experiment assignment, and attribution window.
   - Define the primary conversion as eligible exposed users/accounts reaching first paid conversion within the pre-specified two-week read window; do not count refunds, failed payments, duplicate invoices, or pre-exposure payments as new conversions.

Cross-event integrity checks
- Every signup start, checkout start, and paid conversion in the primary cohort must join to exactly one eligible pricing-page assignment and must carry the resolved variant or a deterministic assignment join.
- Reconcile pageviews → exposures → signup starts → checkout starts → paid conversions by day and by arm. Investigate missing or duplicated joins before interpreting the metric.
- Check event arrival lag separately from event occurrence time; late-arriving events must be backfilled without changing the original event timestamp.
- Compare client and warehouse counts, verify flag-resolution counts against PostHog, and retain the raw query/CSV used for the read.
- The independent Owen cohort cut matched the rerun, so the final negative result was not attributed to a query bug or PostHog failure.

Segment cuts required in the analysis CSV
The CSV should include the full cohort cut and conversion-by-day, with each row carrying arm, eligible/exposed population, numerator, denominator, conversion rate, absolute difference, and confidence/p-value inputs. Break out at minimum:
- plan/tier: Starter vs Growth;
- customer type: new-logo vs existing customer;
- churn status / churn slice, including the requested churn breakdown;
- self-serve eligibility and any excluded-plan audit row;
- treatment vs holdout overall and by day since exposure;
- signup start, checkout start, and paid conversion rates at each funnel step;
- exposure date and pre/post rollback timing.

The technical CSV sent to Daniela included the complete cohort breakdown, conversion-by-day data, and explicit p-value calculations so the read could be traced end to end. Do not collapse these cuts into a single blended number, and do not infer a segment result where the CSV has no eligible denominator.

Result

Postmortem: pricing-page revision

Hypothesis
A clearer pricing-page package—simplified layout, explicit value-per-seat framing, and less visual clutter—would lift started checkouts per pricing-page visitor and, more importantly, signup-to-paid conversion for self-serve Starter and Growth users. Population and assignment
- Eligible audience: self-serve Starter and Growth users only. Enterprise and other non-target plans were excluded.
- Treatment: pricing page revision rendered when pricing_page_2023q2_rev resolved to treatment.
- Control / holdout: the same eligible audience with the flag resolving to the unchanged pricing page.
- Allocation: 50% treatment / 50% holdout during the live window.
- Assignment must be persistent at the account/user level for the read; users must not move arms between pageviews.
- Primary analysis cohort: eligible users with a pricing-page exposure during the live window, analyzed by assigned arm; exclude pre-exposure conversions and post-rollback exposures from the primary read.

Exact PostHog exposure rule
The historical launch rule was: Starter + Growth only, with a 50% rollout on pricing_page_2023q2_rev. In plain terms, include only self-serve accounts whose plan/tier is Starter or Growth, then randomly assign 50% to the revision and retain the other 50% as holdout. Exclude all other plans and any users/accounts outside the self-serve audience. The available flag record stores the audience as “Starter + Growth only”; the underlying PostHog property key/value expression is not present in the experiment registry, so it is not reproduced here as an invented field name.

- Launch: 2023-03-07.
- Live read: 50% traffic for approximately two weeks.
- Decision: powered two-week read was complete by 2023-03-20; rollback was executed rather than extending the test.

arguments.title: Helio Start Q4 controlled beta — operating shape
arguments.body:
Helio Start Q4 controlled beta — operating shape

Purpose and decision boundary

This is the canonical operating shape for the Q4 Helio Start controlled beta. It translates the Q4 decision into a shared operating path so staff leads use the same terms and boundaries.

The decision is to continue Helio Start only as a capped, non-public, invite-only controlled beta for a narrow cohort. The beta is an operating-safety and repeatability test: can this constrained path work with clear eligibility, conservative lifecycle handling, reliable instrumentation, and manageable support load?

This document is not a GA plan, a pricing-page plan, a public-launch plan, a revenue forecast, or a new team charter. More invitations, activation, or positive learning do not by themselves authorize widening the beta or changing its public posture. Any expansion is a separate decision requiring explicit evidence.

1. Eligible accounts

An account may be considered for invitation only when all of the following are true:

- Fewer than 50 seats.
- Complete eligibility information is recorded before review.
- Simple deployment and a first-week integration path.
- Clear workspace-administrator ownership, with the administrator identified and able to complete the required admin steps.
- No requirement for manual, custom, exception, or otherwise non-standard billing.
- No requirement for migration, historical contact-list transfer, CSV import, or other import assistance before the first integration.
- The account passes manual review against the support and lifecycle boundaries in this document.

Seat count alone is not an eligibility decision. Activity, ARR, general customer fit, invite acceptance, or activation cannot substitute for missing eligibility evidence.

Accounts with uncertainty should be routed to Customer Success for review or assisted handling rather than inferred into the self-serve beta path. Self-serve and assisted accounts must remain distinguishable in the records and in reporting.

2. Explicit unsupported list

The Q4 controlled beta does not support:

- Public or open access, general availability, or broad rollout.
- Placement on the public pricing page, a pricing-page experiment, or any public acquisition surface.
- Paid acquisition or a launch campaign.
- Q3 revenue credit, a Q4 launch forecast, a revenue guarantee, or language implying forecastable conversion.
- Manual, custom, annual-exception, or other non-standard billing arrangements.
- Migration, historical-data transfer, contact-list migration, CSV import, or import assistance as part of the self-serve beta path.
- Accounts without clear administrative ownership.
- Complex permission, multi-party, agency-shared-admin, or other setups that require support beyond the defined simple path.
- Support-heavy onboarding that cannot be handled through the documented path or an explicitly owned assisted route.
- A live state-changing lifecycle branch based on an inferred entitlement, support state, plan name, invite acceptance, or activation event.
- Treating more invitations, activation, or early usage as permission to widen access.

Unsupported requests are paused and routed to a supported assisted path when appropriate. They are tracked separately from controlled-beta self-serve metrics; they are not counted as beta failures or silently converted into eligible cases.

3. Measurement and dashboard shape

The Q4 read should answer whether the bounded operating path is safe and repeatable. It should not be used to claim representative demand, scalable support, launch readiness, technical ownership verification, or revenue conversion.

Dashboard sections:

- Candidate funnel: candidates identified, records complete, manual-review outcomes, invited accounts, and reasons for hold or assisted routing.
- Cohort shape: invited, active, and self-serve versus assisted accounts, with the eligibility definition visible on every cut.
- Activation: activation definition v3 and first-integration attempts/results, reported separately for self-serve and assisted accounts. Do not place a first-paid-month or paid-conversion column on the controlled-beta view.
- Operating safety: support questions per active beta account, category mix, and concentration by account. Preserve distinct categories for permissions/admin roles, imports/history/CSV expectations, billing expectations, and docs/API setup rather than collapsing them into generic onboarding.
- Lifecycle evidence: delivery and engagement for the two approved educational touches, with no implication that engagement changes entitlement or state.
- Data quality: entitlement state, support state, and backfill completeness. Missing support state is pending for up to 10 minutes, then unresolved as instrumentation lag; neither state is inferred. Pending and unresolved rows remain in a separate QA count and are excluded from state-dependent rates.
- Boundary outcomes: assisted routes, unsupported requests, escalations, and concentration of support burden.

Helio Start activation, retained mid-segment results, and Expansion Assist remain separate cohorts and readout streams. Expansion Assist is not a Helio Start proof point or a reason to widen this beta.

The keep-capped versus reconsider-later decision requires explicit evidence that concentrated support burdens are manageable, the admin-proof step reduces avoidable handoffs, and the operating path can be repeated without weakening the unsupported list. Reconsideration is a separate decision, not an automatic result of dashboard movement.

4. Lifecycle boundaries

The approved lifecycle path is conservative and non-state-changing:

- After workspace creation: one setup-checklist education touch, subject to manual review.
- Before the first integration: one first-integration preparation explainer, subject to manual review.
- The touches may clarify the required administrator and the documented setup path. They may not grant access, change entitlement, trigger billing, promise unsupported help, or route an account into a different state based on a proxy.
- No live Customer.io branch may make a state-changing decision for this beta. Draft or mapped lifecycle work stays in copy-and-boundary review until separately approved.
- When admin ownership, billing, import/migration needs, permissions, or support burden are unclear, pause the self-serve path and route to Customer Success for an owned assisted response.
- Routine integration questions use docs-first help. Support-heavy or unsupported cases use the assisted route and are reported separately.
- Lifecycle language should be customer-protective and neutral: assisted setup is a supported route, not an account failure or a failed screening outcome.

5. Instrumentation responsibilities

- Owen: own the Q4 beta dashboard and readout structure; maintain candidate and active-account views; keep Helio Start activation separate from retained mid-segment and Expansion Assist; report support load per active account, category mix, and account concentration.
- Daniela: own event taxonomy, entitlement and support-state instrumentation, source-of-truth mapping, QA evidence, and backfill evidence; ensure the data path does not infer entitlement from plan name or other proxies; maintain the pending/unresolved QA treatment.
- Ines: keep the two educational lifecycle touches within the conservative, non-state-changing fork; maintain copy and boundary review; do not ship proxy automation or live state-changing branches.
- Customer Success: provide docs-first routine help, own assisted routing for uncertainty and support-heavy cases, and record support category and route so these cases remain visible and separate.
- Riley: perform the final guardrail check on eligibility, unsupported boundaries, lifecycle behavior, cohort separation, and evidence sufficiency before invitations or any scope change.

Each owner is responsible for evidence within this operating shape, not for creating a broader mandate or implying that the beta is a launch program.

6. Language that is not allowed

Do not describe Helio Start as:

- “launched,” “launching,” “GA,” “generally available,” “open,” or “public.”
- A “pricing-page experiment,” “pricing-page plan,” “acquisition motion,” or “paid-growth channel.”
- A “Q4 launch,” “revenue wedge,” “committed with risk,” “forecastable launch,” or Q3 revenue guarantee.
- A broad demand test, representative market read, scalable support proof, or evidence that the admin path is solved.
- A new team charter, permanent operating model, or standing cross-functional program.
- An account “failure,” “rejection,” or “refusal” when the appropriate description is that the request is outside the supported beta path and is being routed to assisted support.
- “Upgrade your plan to unlock team automations” or other plan/entitlement language in a controlled-beta education touch.

Use these terms instead:

- “Capped, invite-only controlled beta.”
- “Selected accounts that meet the documented eligibility gate.”
- “Supported self-serve path” and “assisted route.”
- “Paused pending eligibility or support-boundary review.”
- “Operating-safety and repeatability evidence.”
- “Keep capped versus reconsider later,” with the evidence required for reconsideration stated explicitly.

This vocabulary is part of the operating boundary. It should be used consistently in staff updates, dashboards, lifecycle copy, support notes, and readouts.

The initial plan for Riley’s institutional document, **“Mid-segment churn investigation Feb-Apr 2023 -- what we learned,”** was an evidence-first outline covering:

The intended structure was a **chronological, method-first investigation narrative**: start with what was observed, lay out the competing explanations, show how each was tested or ruled out over time, explain the onboarding experiment and the decision threshold, then close with the segmentation change and reusable lessons. The writing was meant to stay factual—using ticket IDs, cohort dates, and explicit ownership/checks—to prevent the investigation from turning into folklore.

messages.content:
1. Who is eligible for Helio Start?

Helio Start is designed for straightforward teams with fewer than 50 users, but team size alone does not determine eligibility. Our eligibility check also confirms that you have administrative access, a supported billing arrangement, and a first integration you can connect within your first week. If your setup meets these conditions, you can continue through the self-guided path.

2. Does Helio Start include data imports or migrations?

Helio Start supports a straightforward first integration and self-guided setup. Historical imports, CSV uploads, and migrations are not included in the self-guided Helio Start path. If you need help bringing existing data over, our onboarding team can review your setup and guide you to the appropriate assisted option.

3. Can I use any payment arrangement with Helio Start?

Helio Start is available with supported billing arrangements shown during the eligibility and checkout process. Custom terms, manual invoicing, and other exceptions may require review and are not guaranteed to be available through Helio Start. If you have a specific billing requirement, contact onboarding so we can confirm the right path before you begin.

4. What happens if my setup needs additional help?

Assisted routing is an intentional way to match your setup with the right onboarding experience. If you need migration or import help, have a more complex permissions or administrator setup, require billing review, or do not meet the self-guided criteria, we will connect you with onboarding before setup begins. This is not a penalty or loss of access—it helps ensure that your team gets the appropriate support for its needs.

arguments.title: Helio Start connector-access gap: authority and evidence cue review
arguments.hypothesis: A connector-specific authority question or evidence cue, applied after current eligibility is established and without using connector choice as an eligibility proxy, can identify applicants who administer Helio but cannot authenticate their selected integration. The cue may distinguish failed authentication from other nonactivation causes while preserving eligibility boundaries and avoiding collection of passwords or secrets.
arguments.metric_of_record: Among the 31 admitted nonactivators in the completed audit, count and rate with confirmed failed-authentication evidence, reported separately for the 18 credential-readiness cases and the other 13 cases; also report cue capture rate, false-positive/unclear rate, and subsequent activation outcome. Connector choice is descriptive only and is not an eligibility criterion.
arguments.cohort_scope: Initial review cohort: 31 admitted Helio Start nonactivators from the completed audit, partitioned into 18 credential-readiness cases and 13 other cases. Preserve the two groups as distinct analytic and support categories.
arguments.timeline: Created 2024-04-18. Initial review and wording/instrumentation/routing design only; no live check is approved until review is complete.
arguments.body:
Purpose
Assess whether a connector-specific authority question or evidence cue can identify an access/authentication gap among already-admitted Helio Start applicants. This is an investigation brief, not approval to change eligibility or launch a live check.

Guardrails
- Preserve current eligibility boundaries.
- Do not use connector choice itself as a proxy for eligibility, authority, readiness, or likely activation.
- Do not collect passwords, tokens, API keys, credentials, or other secrets.
- Treat any live check as unapproved until its customer-facing wording, instrumentation, data handling, and routing consequences are reviewed.
- Keep credential-readiness cases distinct from the other nonactivation cases; do not collapse them into a generic onboarding category.
- A reported authority/access cue is evidence to investigate, not an automatic exclusion or eligibility decision.

Initial cohort and ownership
- 31 admitted nonactivators from the completed audit.
- 18 credential-readiness cases: retain as a separate cohort and support category.
- 13 other cases: retain as a separate comparison category; do not assume they are connector-access cases.
- Owen owns denominator definition, cohort accounting, outcome analysis, and comparison of cue results across the two groups.
- Customer Success will code failed-authentication evidence and test customer-readable wording, including whether the question distinguishes inability to authenticate from lack of authority, missing permissions, setup confusion, or another failure mode.
- Daniela will assess what can be captured reliably before setup, including the timing, source, completeness, and operational meaning of any response or evidence cue.

Proposed review approach
1. Confirm the audit denominator and case labels for all 31 admitted nonactivators before introducing a cue.
2. Define a minimal, connector-specific question or evidence cue that asks about administrative authority or authentication readiness without requesting secrets. Keep connector selection descriptive and analytically controlled, not an eligibility input.
3. Have Customer Success review wording for clarity, customer burden, refusal risk, and the distinction between self-reported authority and observed failed authentication.
4. Have Daniela document pre-setup capture feasibility, missingness, retention, and whether the signal arrives early enough to affect support routing without changing eligibility.
5. Define evidence codes and an explicit unknown/unclear state before coding. At minimum, separate confirmed failed authentication, permission/role limitation, missing credential readiness, setup misunderstanding, other nonactivation cause, and insufficient evidence.
6. Specify instrumentation and routing review requirements before any live test: event names, denominator inclusion/exclusion, data minimization, access controls, support handoff, and the consequence of an unanswered or negative response.
7. Owen will compare cue classifications with activation outcomes and support contacts, reporting counts and rates for 18 credential-readiness versus 13 other cases. Results should show denominator, effect size, cohort stability, and uncertainty; direction alone is not a rollout decision.

Decision status
Open investigation. No eligibility change, applicant block, or live check is approved.

Unresolved design questions
- What exact authority distinction is needed: administer Helio, administer the selected external system, authorize an OAuth/app connection, or complete a role/permission step?
- Should the cue ask about authority, ability to authenticate, or both, and in what order to avoid implying that connector choice determines eligibility?
- What customer-readable wording distinguishes failed authentication from insufficient permissions, missing admin ownership, and general setup difficulty?
- What non-secret evidence can a customer provide, if any, and how can it be validated without collecting credentials or exposing sensitive account data?
- Which connectors support a reliable pre-setup signal, and where would the signal be unavailable or misleading?
- Can the cue be captured before setup without adding friction that changes the admitted cohort or selectively suppresses difficult cases?
- What constitutes confirmed, probable, unclear, or absent failed-authentication evidence, and who adjudicates ambiguous cases?
- How should unanswered, refused, or “I am not the admin” responses be routed without changing eligibility boundaries or creating an automatic denial path?
- What instrumentation is required to connect cue responses, failed-authentication evidence, support handling, and activation outcomes while preserving the original audit denominator?
- What is the appropriate comparison or baseline for the 13 other cases, given that connector choice cannot be used as a proxy and the audit cohort is small?
- What review is required for wording, instrumentation, privacy/data handling, and routing before a live check can be considered?
- What result would justify a follow-up design iteration, and what result would show that the cue is too noisy or operationally costly to pursue?

arguments.body:
# Helio Start connector-access investigation brief

## Live design (effective 2024-04-23)

The reviewed connector-access change is live in the Helio Start intake reached from the public pricing page. The connector-authentication question is a distinct signal from Helio workspace-admin proof:

- Daniela stores the connector-authentication answer separately from Helio admin proof.
- A definite **Yes** continues through the otherwise unchanged Helio Start eligibility checks.
- **No** and **Not sure** remain pending and route to assistance before workspace admission.
- Applicants must not enter passwords, tokens, API keys, or other secrets; the intake captures only the permitted answer/state.
- A Helio admin-proof value does not independently unlock a connector-specific path, and an unanswered, refused, unclear, or unsure answer is not silently treated as false or as a pass.

## Routing and lifecycle behavior

While connector proof is pending, Ines prevents connection prompts and other setup-state-changing lifecycle messages. Customer Success routes pending cases to assistance using the updated routing instructions and resolves the appropriate administrator/connector-authority path before admission or setup. Safe educational copy remains separate from state-changing messaging and does not authorize workspace admission, routing, or setup transitions.

A Yes response proceeds only after the existing eligibility checks remain satisfied. No and Not sure do not become automatic denials; they stay pending for assisted review. The response is retained for auditability alongside, but not merged with, workspace-admin proof and subsequent support/routing outcomes.

## Operating owners

- Daniela: owns the separate connector-authentication field and its capture/instrumentation, distinct from Helio admin-proof evidence.
- Ines: owns lifecycle guards, including suppressing connection prompts while proof is pending.
- Customer Success: owns pending-case routing and assistance instructions, including resolution of permissions, authority, and ownership questions.
- Owen: owns the noncausal evaluation plan, denominator definitions, outcome comparisons, and interpretation of support/routing effects.

## Unchanged boundaries

This change does not widen eligibility, convert the flow to general availability, or make connector choice an eligibility proxy. The existing Helio Start checks and guarded operating model remain in force. Agencies or outside administrators, unresolved ownership, manual or custom billing, imports, migrations, unsupported permissions, support-heavy setup, and other existing route-out conditions remain unchanged. Such cases stay outside clean self-serve setup and follow the appropriate assisted path. No secrets are collected, and no state-changing branch is allowed when entitlement, ownership, support state, or routing is unknown.

## Owen's evaluation plan

Evaluate this as an operational and descriptive investigation, not a causal launch or expansion test. Owen will:

1. Define the denominator as eligible starts under the existing Helio Start rules, keeping the connector-answer states and route-out reasons mutually visible rather than collapsing them into a single onboarding bucket.
2. Report definite Yes, No, Not sure, unanswered/refused/unclear, and routed-out or assisted cases separately; preserve the distinction between workspace-admin proof and connector authority/readiness.
3. Compare first integration within seven days, time to setup/admission, pending duration, assistance/routing rate, support contacts, and failure states, with pre-admission contacts and assisted setup kept separate from clean self-serve outcomes.
4. Retain the initial nonactivator diagnostic split where applicable: 31 admitted nonactivators, including 18 credential-readiness cases and 13 other cases, without treating that observational split as a causal estimate.
5. Check cohort dates, denominator integrity, missingness, refusal/unknown handling, lifecycle suppression, and support-load concentration before interpreting directional differences.
6. Label any observed association as descriptive. No result alone authorizes broader access, weakened refusal boundaries, public self-serve claims, or a causal conclusion; continuation or follow-up decisions require stabilized cuts and review of support and lifecycle risk.

The brief records the live implementation and its guardrails; it is not an approval to remove existing route-out conditions or to infer that connector access causes activation.

Helio Start capped paid-acquisition proposal — Q2 2026 working draft

Working status and authorization boundary

This is a working proposal for a possible capped Q2 2026 paid-acquisition test. It is not an approval, launch authorization, budget approval, paid-traffic authorization, pipeline target, forecast input, or acquisition claim.

Priya has authorized preparation of this draft. That authorization is limited to preparing the proposal; it does not authorize launch or spend. Any paid test would require separate decisions and approvals, including a separate budget approval. Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026.

Purpose

Translate the two qualifying mature-cohort readouts into a decision-ready, bounded proposal without treating the evidence as causal, scalable acquisition economics, pipeline contribution, or forecast credit. All choices below remain open unless explicitly identified as an existing operating rule or evidence condition.

Evidence basis: two qualifying mature cohorts

The reopening evidence condition is satisfied: two consecutive mature cohorts each had fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes, and neither cohort had an unsupported case enter the admitted path. This satisfies the condition for reopening consideration of a capped proposal; it does not approve the proposal or authorize a paid test.

Cohort 1 — January 27, 2026 certification
- Denominator: 86 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows.
- Mutually exclusive day-90 statuses: 66 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, and 4 on billing hold.
- Gross billed cash: $100,840.
- Refund-adjusted collected cash: $94,760.
- Account-level support effort: 19 minutes median; 84 minutes at p90.
- Support threshold: 4 of 86 accounts, or 4.7%, exceeded 90 support minutes.
- Path integrity: no unsupported case entered the admitted path.

Cohort 2 — February 24, 2026 certification
- Denominator: 91 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows.
- Mutually exclusive day-90 statuses: 71 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, and 4 on billing hold.
- Gross billed cash: $108,230.
- Refund-adjusted collected cash: $102,410.
- Account-level support effort: 18 minutes median; 79 minutes at p90.
- Support threshold: 3 of 91 accounts, or 3.3%, exceeded 90 support minutes.
- Path integrity: no unsupported case entered the admitted path.

Maturity and source limits

- These are complete day-90 windows. Any immature or later window must remain separate and must not be silently folded into the mature read.
- Mature-window status shares are not final long-run retention.
- The exact underlying cohort dates remain missing or unresolved in the certified source record; the certification labels above identify the January 27 and February 24 certification checkpoints, not a reconstructed cohort-start date.
- The two cohorts are descriptive operating evidence. They do not establish causal lift, CAC, payback, scalable acquisition economics, revenue impact, or future-cohort performance.
- Keep statuses mutually exclusive and report day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort together. Do not reduce the evidence gate to a single conversion or cash number.
- The mature-cohort evidence is limited to the admitted-path scope. It does not support conclusions about manual-billing, import, migration, or agency paths that were excluded from the admitted path.

Existing rules and boundaries preserved

The proposal does not change the existing operating rules. The following remain in force:

- Eligibility: retain the approved Helio Start eligibility definition and any required preflight checks; do not broaden eligibility for paid traffic based on the mature-cohort results.
- Refusal: existing refusal conditions and fail-closed handling remain unchanged.
- Connector access: the proposal does not grant, expand, or infer connector access.
- External authority: existing external-authority and ownership requirements remain mandatory. External authority is not blanket permission to contact or message; governed state and applicable messaging rules still control.
- Lifecycle: existing lifecycle states, suppression, renewal/adoption handling, and other lifecycle protections remain unchanged.
- Instrumentation: preserve the existing path-selection, eligibility, admission, and support-routing event taxonomy and required observability. No paid test should begin without instrumentation validation and an accountable source owner.
- Admission: no unsupported case may enter the admitted path. The existing admitted-path definition and refusal handling remain unchanged.
- Support routing: existing support-routing rules, governed handoffs, and escalation paths remain unchanged. Paid traffic does not bypass support triage or create an automatic handoff.
- Organic boundary: Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026. No paid traffic is authorized before that boundary.
- Commercial boundaries: do not assign pipeline, revenue, acquisition, or forecast credit to this evidence or to a future test unless separately approved, defined, measured, and certified.

Open decision 1 — Traffic cap

Decision needed: the maximum paid traffic volume, exposure rate, duration, and any pacing or concentration limits for a possible Q2 test.

Not settled:
- No traffic quantity, percentage, weekly volume, flight length, or pacing schedule is approved.
- No channel mix or allocation is approved.
- No assumption may be made that a capped test will launch once the evidence gate is satisfied.

Required decision record: the accountable approver, exact cap, time basis, audience allocation, pacing method, and conditions for reducing or ending traffic.

Open decision 2 — Budget request

Decision needed: whether to request a budget at all and, if so, the amount, funding source, duration, spend controls, and approval path.

Not settled:
- No dollar amount, test budget, contingency, or spend ceiling is proposed as final.
- No budget is approved or committed.
- Refund-adjusted cohort cash is evidence context, not a funding source, budget justification, or forecast assumption.

Required decision record: requested amount, accounting treatment, approver, spending authority, test period, and confirmation that separate budget approval has been obtained before any launch.

Open decision 3 — Audience and channel

Decision needed: which audience(s) and paid channel(s), if any, could be considered without changing Helio Start eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, admission, or support-routing rules.

Not settled:
- No audience, targeting rule, channel, creative, landing path, or placement is selected.
- No transfer of organic eligibility or external-authority state into paid-contact permission is assumed.
- Any proposed audience mapping, suppression list, source freshness check, and destination must be separately reviewed.

Required decision record: audience definition, exclusion and suppression rules, channel, destination path, consent/contact basis, owner, and rollback mechanism.

Open decision 4 — Success measure

Decision needed: the primary success measure, secondary measures, denominator, maturity window, attribution method, and decision threshold for the proposal or any eventual test.

Not settled:
- No CAC, payback, conversion, retention, paid-active, cash, or support metric is designated as the primary success measure.
- The two mature cohorts do not establish a paid-acquisition benchmark.
- No success measure may convert descriptive organic evidence into causal lift, revenue impact, pipeline contribution, or forecast credit.

Required decision record: predeclared primary metric, supporting metrics, eligible and admitted denominators, complete outcome window, attribution limits, minimum evidence requirements, and decision rule.

Open decision 5 — Support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails

Existing evidence gate to preserve exactly:
- Each of two consecutive mature cohorts must have fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes.
- No unsupported case may enter the admitted path.

Decision needed for any paid test: how these guardrails will be monitored in paid traffic, what denominator and maturity rules apply, whether additional support-capacity limits are required, and who can stop traffic.

Not settled:
- No paid-test support threshold, capacity reserve, contact-rate limit, escalation threshold, or audience-specific guardrail is chosen.
- The mature-cohort evidence does not establish that paid traffic will carry the same support burden.
- Any additional guardrail must supplement, not weaken or replace, the existing two-cohort evidence condition and unsupported-admission prohibition.

Required decision record: support metric definitions, denominator, reporting cadence, capacity owner, escalation route, immediate-stop condition for unsupported admission, and treatment of unresolved classifications.

Open decision 6 — Monitoring and stop rules

Decision needed: monitoring cadence, dashboards and source owners, launch checks, incident process, rollback authority, and predeclared stop or pause rules.

Not settled:
- No launch date, monitoring frequency, stop threshold, pause duration, or restart rule is approved.
- No person is yet designated here as the sole rollback authority for a paid test.
- No test should proceed without validated instrumentation, readable operator views, governed state, and a tested rollback path.

Non-negotiable conditions to preserve in the decision record:
- Stop or pause immediately if an unsupported case enters the admitted path.
- Stop or pause if required eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, admission, or support-routing state cannot be observed or reconciled.
- Do not continue through stale, conflicting, deactivated-admin, or otherwise fail-closed state.

Required decision record: prelaunch checks, live monitors, thresholds, alert destinations, incident owner, stop authority, rollback steps, restart criteria, and post-test review owner.

Open decision 7 — Refund-adjusted cash treatment

Evidence treatment to preserve:
- Cohort 1: $100,840 gross billed cash and $94,760 refund-adjusted collected cash.
- Cohort 2: $108,230 gross billed cash and $102,410 refund-adjusted collected cash.
- Gross billed cash must not stand in for cash retained after refunds.

Decision needed: how refund-adjusted cash should be reported in any proposal or test readout, including the accounting definition, observation window, refund handling, and whether it is descriptive context or a governed test metric.

Not settled:
- Refund-adjusted collected cash is not designated as a success threshold, unit-economics conclusion, revenue forecast, or budget-recovery promise.
- No payback, profitability, revenue, pipeline, or forecast treatment is approved.

Required decision record: metric owner, source of truth, refund window and inclusion rules, reconciliation method, reporting cadence, and explicit separation from pipeline and forecast treatment.

Open decision 8 — Decision owners

Known status:
- Priya authorized preparation of this working draft. Her authorization does not approve launch or budget.
- The decision owners for traffic cap, budget request, audience/channel, success measure, support guardrails, monitoring/stop rules, and cash treatment remain to be explicitly confirmed.
- Owen and Customer Success own certification of the mature-cohort source evidence.
- Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership; this draft does not create forecast credit.
- Tomás Vega retains final board-narrative ownership; this draft does not constitute board approval.

Decision needed: assign a named accountable owner and required approvers for each open decision, plus the launch/no-launch authority, source-certification owner, instrumentation owner, support-routing owner, finance/accounting owner, and rollback authority.

Not settled:
- No placeholder assignment in this section is a final operating decision.
- No decision owner may waive the existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, admission, or support-routing rules.

Revenue, pipeline, and forecast treatment

Exclude pipeline or forecast credit. The two mature cohorts are descriptive evidence for reconsidering a bounded proposal, not evidence of pipeline contribution, forecastable demand, incremental revenue, paid-channel performance, or a commercial commitment. Any future test readout must preserve the same exclusions unless separately approved and certified with its own design, denominator, window, and ownership.

Next decision gate

Before this can become an approved launch plan, the open decisions must be resolved explicitly, source and instrumentation readiness must be verified, the March 31 organic-only boundary must have passed, and separate budget and launch approvals must be recorded. Until then, this document remains a working proposal only.

arguments.body:
# Helio Start connector-access investigation brief

## Live design (effective 2024-04-23)

The reviewed connector-access change is live in the Helio Start intake reached from the public pricing page. The connector-authentication question is a distinct signal from Helio workspace-admin proof:

- Daniela stores the connector-authentication answer separately from Helio admin proof.
- A definite **Yes** continues through the otherwise unchanged Helio Start eligibility checks.
- **No** and **Not sure** remain pending and route to assistance before workspace admission.
- Applicants must not enter passwords, tokens, API keys, or other secrets; the intake captures only the permitted answer/state.
- A Helio admin-proof value does not independently unlock a connector-specific path, and an unanswered, refused, unclear, or unsure answer is not silently treated as false or as a pass.

## Routing and lifecycle behavior

While connector proof is pending, Ines prevents connection prompts and other setup-state-changing lifecycle messages. Customer Success routes pending cases to assistance using the updated routing instructions and resolves the appropriate administrator/connector-authority path before admission or setup. Safe educational copy remains separate from state-changing messaging and does not authorize workspace admission, routing, or setup transitions.

A Yes response proceeds only after the existing eligibility checks remain satisfied. No and Not sure do not become automatic denials; they stay pending for assisted review. The response is retained for auditability alongside, but not merged with, workspace-admin proof and subsequent support/routing outcomes.

## Operating owners

- Daniela: owns the separate connector-authentication field and its capture/instrumentation, distinct from Helio admin-proof evidence.
- Ines: owns lifecycle guards, including suppressing connection prompts while proof is pending.
- Customer Success: owns pending-case routing and assistance instructions, including resolution of permissions, authority, and ownership questions.
- Owen: owns the noncausal evaluation plan, denominator definitions, outcome comparisons, and interpretation of support/routing effects.

## Unchanged boundaries

This change does not widen eligibility, convert the flow to general availability, or make connector choice an eligibility proxy. The existing Helio Start checks and guarded operating model remain in force. Agencies or outside administrators, unresolved ownership, manual or custom billing, imports, migrations, unsupported permissions, support-heavy setup, and other existing route-out conditions remain unchanged. Such cases stay outside clean self-serve setup and follow the appropriate assisted path. No secrets are collected, and no state-changing branch is allowed when entitlement, ownership, support state, or routing is unknown.

## Owen's evaluation plan

Evaluate this as an operational and descriptive investigation, not a causal launch or expansion test. Owen will:

1. Define the denominator as eligible starts under the existing Helio Start rules, keeping the connector-answer states and route-out reasons mutually visible rather than collapsing them into a single onboarding bucket.
2. Report definite Yes, No, Not sure, unanswered/refused/unclear, and routed-out or assisted cases separately; preserve the distinction between workspace-admin proof and connector authority/readiness.
3. Compare first integration within seven days, time to setup/admission, pending duration, assistance/routing rate, support contacts, and failure states, with pre-admission contacts and assisted setup kept separate from clean self-serve outcomes.
4. Retain the initial nonactivator diagnostic split where applicable: 31 admitted nonactivators, including 18 credential-readiness cases and 13 other cases, without treating that observational split as a causal estimate.
5. Check cohort dates, denominator integrity, missingness, refusal/unknown handling, lifecycle suppression, and support-load concentration before interpreting directional differences.
6. Label any observed association as descriptive. No result alone authorizes broader access, weakened refusal boundaries, public self-serve claims, or a causal conclusion; continuation or follow-up decisions require stabilized cuts and review of support and lifecycle risk.

The brief records the live implementation and its guardrails; it is not an approval to remove existing route-out conditions or to infer that connector access causes activation.

arguments.body:
Purpose and approved question

In Monday's one-on-one on 2024-07-08, Priya approved a narrow diagnostic question: among recent Helio Start applicants who expressed connector-access uncertainty, which uncertainty concerns:

1. Control of existing credentials
2. Supported-connector availability
3. Security approval timing
4. An expectation of same-day setup

Sample

- Start with eight recent applicant interactions.
- De-identify all interactions before review or inclusion in the readout.
- Record only the interaction evidence needed to apply the coding dimensions; omit names, direct identifiers, and unnecessary account details.
- Preserve overlap when an interaction contains more than one concern.
- Preserve uncodable or ambiguous cases explicitly rather than forcing a category.

Coding dimensions

For each interaction, code evidence for each of the four dimensions independently:

- Credential control: concern about who controls, can access, owns, or must provide existing credentials.
- Supported-connector availability: concern about whether the needed connector or integration is supported/available.
- Security approval timing: concern about the timing or duration of security, IT, compliance, or administrative approval.
- Same-day setup expectation: expectation that setup or connection should be completed on the same day.

Completed descriptive coding of the eight excerpts

The eight excerpts were coded as follows. Codes reflect only what the excerpt supports; multiple codes are retained only when the wording supports both issues.

| Excerpt | Credential control / usable-credential uncertainty | Supported-connector availability | Security-approval timing | Same-day setup expectation | Evidence note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Yes | — | — | — | Admin is unavailable; the applicant asks whether someone else can connect Salesforce using the admin's login. |
| B | — | Supported connector stated | Yes | — | The warehouse connector is listed in the docs, while security approval for the service account is still pending. |
| C | — | Question about unsupported in-house connector | — | — | The applicant asks whether an in-house event bus is supported; this is uncertainty, not confirmation of an unsupported product limitation. |
| D | — | — | — | Yes | The applicant expects the workspace and connector to be live today after clicking Start. |
| E | Yes | — | — | — | Procurement controls the credential vault and will not release credentials to the growth team. |
| F | — | — | Yes | — | Security review is scheduled for next Thursday; the applicant asks to complete admission before connection. |
| G | Yes | HubSpot stated as available | — | — | An admin can authorize HubSpot, but the applicant does not know which Helio permissions are required; this is permission/usable-credential uncertainty, not an unsupported-connector claim. |
| H | Yes | Supported source stated | — | — | The data source is supported, but the person controlling its credentials has not joined the project. |

Descriptive counts for this eight-excerpt sample

- Credential-control / usable-credential uncertainty: 4 of 8.
- Security-approval timing: 2 of 8.
- Question about an unsupported in-house connector: 1 of 8. This remains an applicant question; the coding does not establish that the connector is actually unsupported or that Helio has a product limitation.
- Same-day workspace-and-connector setup expectation: 1 of 8.

These counts are descriptive only. They are based on eight excerpts, do not estimate prevalence, do not establish a product defect, and should not be generalized beyond this small sample. The counts are not intended to form a forced single-category distribution; any overlap is retained only where an excerpt explicitly supports both issues. Confirmed-supported references in B, G, and H are recorded as evidence context and are not treated as unsupported-connector cases.

Bounded review questions for Priya

1. Is clearer pre-application language about who must control or provide usable credentials worth testing?
2. Is supported-connector language sufficiently visible before applicants reach or act on the admission flow?
3. Do same-day workspace-and-connector expectations arise from copy outside the admission flow?

These are bounded review questions, not recommendations or decisions. The descriptive coding should not be used to infer causality, prevalence, admission impact, or a need to change the flow.

Approved bounded follow-up from Priya's 2024-07-15 review

Priya reviewed the eight-excerpt diagnostic and approved one bounded follow-up only: trace the live wording on these three surfaces to determine whether any surface promises same-day workspace or connector setup:

1. The public pricing page.
2. The application confirmation.
3. The Customer Success autoresponder.

Completed implementation and passing fixture — 2024-07-22

- The Customer Success autoresponder now says: `If you're approved, we'll confirm your workspace setup steps and timing by email.`
- The confirmation fixture passes: the replacement appears in the rendered response, and the fixture finds no remaining same-day setup promise.
- The pricing-page wording is unchanged.
- The application-confirmation wording is unchanged.
- The Helio Start admission rule is unchanged.
- This completed implementation and passing fixture close the bounded copy trace; no broader copy audit or admission-flow change is implied.

Evidence boundary for the completed follow-up

The wording trace was a source-verification and narrowly bounded implementation step, not a conclusion that the one same-day expectation proves a product defect. The passing fixture verifies the rendered Customer Success response and absence of a same-day setup promise there; it does not establish causality, prevalence, user comprehension, or product failure. Preserve the distinction between explicit wording, implication, applicant interpretation, and absence of evidence.

Suggested descriptive output

- Eight-row de-identified interaction coding table.
- For each dimension, count of interactions and share of the eight-interaction sample.
- Multi-coded interactions shown as overlapping, not assigned to a single forced primary category.
- Any unclear, missing, or uncodable evidence listed separately.
- Short evidence notes using de-identified wording only.
- Completed bounded copy trace across the three named surfaces, with the autoresponder implementation and passing fixture result recorded explicitly.

Exclusions and guardrails

- Do not reopen, revise, or recommend changing the Helio Start admission rule.
- Do not label uncertainty itself as a product defect.
- Do not treat the single same-day expectation in the eight-excerpt sample as proof of a product defect.
- Do not infer causality, prevalence beyond this eight-interaction sample, or an admission impact.
- Do not turn the descriptive coding or the wording trace into a recommendation to change admission.
- Do not pull Owen back into weekly signoff; this is not an approval queue or a recurring signoff process.
- Keep the follow-up limited to the three named live surfaces; the implementation endpoint is the Customer Success autoresponder correction and its passing confirmation fixture.
- Keep the work limited to the approved diagnostic question, the eight-interaction sample, and the bounded review questions above.

Decision boundary and endpoint

The admission decision remains unchanged. The pricing-page and application-confirmation wording remain unchanged. The Customer Success autoresponder implementation is complete and its confirmation fixture passes. This brief records a coded descriptive read and a completed bounded external-copy trace; it does not authorize an admission-rule change, new routing behavior, or a product decision. Any future decision about admission would be separate from this diagnostic and would require its own explicit review.

arguments.body:
Purpose and approved question

In Monday's one-on-one on 2024-07-08, Priya approved a narrow diagnostic question: among recent Helio Start applicants who expressed connector-access uncertainty, which uncertainty concerns:

1. Control of existing credentials
2. Supported-connector availability
3. Security approval timing
4. An expectation of same-day setup

Sample

- Start with eight recent applicant interactions.
- De-identify all interactions before review or inclusion in the readout.
- Record only the interaction evidence needed to apply the coding dimensions; omit names, direct identifiers, and unnecessary account details.
- Preserve overlap when an interaction contains more than one concern.
- Preserve uncodable or ambiguous cases explicitly rather than forcing a category.

Coding dimensions

For each interaction, code evidence for each of the four dimensions independently:

- Credential control: concern about who controls, can access, owns, or must provide existing credentials.
- Supported-connector availability: concern about whether the needed connector or integration is supported/available.
- Security approval timing: concern about the timing or duration of security, IT, compliance, or administrative approval.
- Same-day setup expectation: expectation that setup or connection should be completed on the same day.

Completed descriptive coding of the eight excerpts

The eight excerpts were coded as follows. Codes reflect only what the excerpt supports; multiple codes are retained only when the wording supports both issues.

| Excerpt | Credential control / usable-credential uncertainty | Supported-connector availability | Security-approval timing | Same-day setup expectation | Evidence note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Yes | — | — | — | Admin is unavailable; the applicant asks whether someone else can connect Salesforce using the admin's login. |
| B | — | Supported connector stated | Yes | — | The warehouse connector is listed in the docs, while security approval for the service account is still pending. |
| C | — | Question about unsupported in-house connector | — | — | The applicant asks whether an in-house event bus is supported; this is uncertainty, not confirmation of an unsupported product limitation. |
| D | — | — | — | Yes | The applicant expects the workspace and connector to be live today after clicking Start. |
| E | Yes | — | — | — | Procurement controls the credential vault and will not release credentials to the growth team. |
| F | — | — | Yes | — | Security review is scheduled for next Thursday; the applicant asks to complete admission before connection. |
| G | Yes | HubSpot stated as available | — | — | An admin can authorize HubSpot, but the applicant does not know which Helio permissions are required; this is permission/usable-credential uncertainty, not an unsupported-connector claim. |
| H | Yes | Supported source stated | — | — | The data source is supported, but the person controlling its credentials has not joined the project. |

Descriptive counts for this eight-excerpt sample

- Credential-control / usable-credential uncertainty: 4 of 8.
- Security-approval timing: 2 of 8.
- Question about an unsupported in-house connector: 1 of 8. This remains an applicant question; the coding does not establish that the connector is actually unsupported or that Helio has a product limitation.
- Same-day workspace-and-connector setup expectation: 1 of 8.

These counts are descriptive only. They are based on eight excerpts, do not estimate prevalence, do not establish a product defect, and should not be generalized beyond this small sample. The counts are not intended to form a forced single-category distribution; any overlap is retained only where an excerpt explicitly supports both issues. Confirmed-supported references in B, G, and H are recorded as evidence context and are not treated as unsupported-connector cases.

Bounded review questions for Priya

1. Is clearer pre-application language about who must control or provide usable credentials worth testing?
2. Is supported-connector language sufficiently visible before applicants reach or act on the admission flow?
3. Do same-day workspace-and-connector expectations arise from copy outside the admission flow?

These are bounded review questions, not recommendations or decisions. The descriptive coding should not be used to infer causality, prevalence, admission impact, or a need to change the flow.

Approved bounded follow-up from Priya's 2024-07-15 review

Priya reviewed the eight-excerpt diagnostic and approved one bounded follow-up only: trace the live wording on these three surfaces to determine whether any surface promises same-day workspace or connector setup:

1. The public pricing page.
2. The application confirmation.
3. The Customer Success autoresponder.

Collection target

Collect the three exact lines by Wednesday, 2024-07-17: one exact line from each surface. Preserve the surrounding surface name and location/context needed to identify where the wording appeared, but do not expand the review into a broader copy audit. Report whether each line explicitly promises same-day workspace setup, same-day connector setup, both, or neither. If a surface contains no such promise, record that explicitly rather than inferring one.

Evidence boundary for the follow-up

The wording trace is a source-verification step, not a conclusion that the one same-day expectation proves a product defect. The result may show whether a live surface contains a same-day promise; it does not by itself establish causality, prevalence, user comprehension, or product failure. Preserve exact wording and distinguish explicit promises from implication, applicant interpretation, or absence of evidence.

Suggested descriptive output

- Eight-row de-identified interaction coding table.
- For each dimension, count of interactions and share of the eight-interaction sample.
- Multi-coded interactions shown as overlapping, not assigned to a single forced primary category.
- Any unclear, missing, or uncodable evidence listed separately.
- Short evidence notes using de-identified wording only.
- A three-line wording trace, with one exact line each from the pricing page, application confirmation, and Customer Success autoresponder, plus an explicit no-promise/unclear notation where applicable.

Exclusions and guardrails

- Do not reopen, revise, or recommend changing the Helio Start admission rule.
- Do not label uncertainty itself as a product defect.
- Do not treat the single same-day expectation in the eight-excerpt sample as proof of a product defect.
- Do not infer causality, prevalence beyond this eight-interaction sample, or an admission impact.
- Do not turn the descriptive coding or the wording trace into a recommendation to change admission.
- Do not pull Owen back into weekly signoff; this is not an approval queue or a recurring signoff process.
- Keep the follow-up limited to the three named live surfaces and the three exact lines targeted by Wednesday, 2024-07-17.
- Keep the work limited to the approved diagnostic question, the eight-interaction sample, and the bounded review questions above.

Decision boundary

The admission decision remains unchanged. This brief produces a coded descriptive read and a bounded external-copy wording trace; it does not authorize an admission-rule change, new routing behavior, or a product decision. Any future decision about admission would be separate from this diagnostic and would require its own explicit review.

CTA block 1 — bounded Helio Start eligibility

Body

Helio Start is for workspaces with a qualifying human admin, current entitlement, supported billing, a straightforward deployment, and a supported connector that can be connected in the first week. Eligibility also depends on the required access and verified authority for the selected connector.

arguments.title: Helio Start Q4 controlled beta — operating shape
arguments.body:
Helio Start Q4 controlled beta — operating shape

Purpose and decision boundary

This is the canonical operating shape for the Q4 Helio Start controlled beta. It translates the Q4 decision into a shared operating path so staff leads use the same terms and boundaries.

The decision is to continue Helio Start only as a capped, non-public, invite-only controlled beta for a narrow cohort. The beta is an operating-safety and repeatability test: can this constrained path work with clear eligibility, conservative lifecycle handling, reliable instrumentation, and manageable support load?

This document is not a GA plan, a pricing-page plan, a public-launch plan, a revenue forecast, or a new team charter. More invitations, activation, or positive learning do not by themselves authorize widening the beta or changing its public posture. Any expansion is a separate decision requiring explicit evidence.

1. Eligible accounts

An account may be considered for invitation only when all of the following are true:

- Fewer than 50 seats.
- Complete eligibility information is recorded before review.
- Simple deployment and a first-week integration path.
- Clear workspace-administrator ownership, with the administrator identified and able to complete the required admin steps.
- No requirement for manual, custom, exception, or otherwise non-standard billing.
- No requirement for migration, historical contact-list transfer, CSV import, or other import assistance before the first integration.
- The account passes manual review against the support and lifecycle boundaries in this document.

Seat count alone is not an eligibility decision. Activity, ARR, general customer fit, invite acceptance, or activation cannot substitute for missing eligibility evidence.

Accounts with uncertainty should be routed to Customer Success for review or assisted handling rather than inferred into the self-serve beta path. Self-serve and assisted accounts must remain distinguishable in the records and in reporting.

2. Explicit unsupported list

The Q4 controlled beta does not support:

- Public or open access, general availability, or broad rollout.
- Placement on the public pricing page, a pricing-page experiment, or any public acquisition surface.
- Paid acquisition or a launch campaign.
- Q3 revenue credit, a Q4 launch forecast, a revenue guarantee, or language implying forecastable conversion.
- Manual, custom, annual-exception, or other non-standard billing arrangements.
- Migration, historical-data transfer, contact-list migration, CSV import, or import assistance as part of the self-serve beta path.
- Accounts without clear administrative ownership.
- Complex permission, multi-party, agency-shared-admin, or other setups that require support beyond the defined simple path.
- Support-heavy onboarding that cannot be handled through the documented path or an explicitly owned assisted route.
- A live state-changing lifecycle branch based on an inferred entitlement, support state, plan name, invite acceptance, or activation event.
- Treating more invitations, activation, or early usage as permission to widen access.

Unsupported requests are paused and routed to a supported assisted path when appropriate. They are tracked separately from controlled-beta self-serve metrics; they are not counted as beta failures or silently converted into eligible cases.

3. Measurement and dashboard shape

The Q4 read should answer whether the bounded operating path is safe and repeatable. It should not be used to claim representative demand, scalable support, launch readiness, technical ownership verification, or revenue conversion.

Dashboard sections:

- Candidate funnel: candidates identified, records complete, manual-review outcomes, invited accounts, and reasons for hold or assisted routing.
- Cohort shape: invited, active, and self-serve versus assisted accounts, with the eligibility definition visible on every cut.
- Activation: activation definition v3 and first-integration attempts/results, reported separately for self-serve and assisted accounts. Do not place a first-paid-month or paid-conversion column on the controlled-beta view.
- Operating safety: support questions per active beta account, category mix, and concentration by account. Preserve distinct categories for permissions/admin roles, imports/history/CSV expectations, billing expectations, and docs/API setup rather than collapsing them into generic onboarding.
- Lifecycle evidence: delivery and engagement for the two approved educational touches, with no implication that engagement changes entitlement or state.
- Data quality: entitlement state, support state, and backfill completeness. Missing support state is pending for up to 10 minutes, then unresolved as instrumentation lag; neither state is inferred. Pending and unresolved rows remain in a separate QA count and are excluded from state-dependent rates.
- Boundary outcomes: assisted routes, unsupported requests, escalations, and concentration of support burden.

Helio Start activation, retained mid-segment results, and Expansion Assist remain separate cohorts and readout streams. Expansion Assist is not a Helio Start proof point or a reason to widen this beta.

The keep-capped versus reconsider-later decision requires explicit evidence that concentrated support burdens are manageable, the admin-proof step reduces avoidable handoffs, and the operating path can be repeated without weakening the unsupported list. Reconsideration is a separate decision, not an automatic result of dashboard movement.

4. Lifecycle boundaries

The approved lifecycle path is conservative and non-state-changing:

- After workspace creation: one setup-checklist education touch, subject to manual review.
- Before the first integration: one first-integration preparation explainer, subject to manual review.
- The touches may clarify the required administrator and the documented setup path. They may not grant access, change entitlement, trigger billing, promise unsupported help, or route an account into a different state based on a proxy.
- No live Customer.io branch may make a state-changing decision for this beta. Draft or mapped lifecycle work stays in copy-and-boundary review until separately approved.
- When admin ownership, billing, import/migration needs, permissions, or support burden are unclear, pause the self-serve path and route to Customer Success for an owned assisted response.
- Routine integration questions use docs-first help. Support-heavy or unsupported cases use the assisted route and are reported separately.
- Lifecycle language should be customer-protective and neutral: assisted setup is a supported route, not an account failure or a failed screening outcome.

5. Instrumentation responsibilities

- Owen: own the Q4 beta dashboard and readout structure; maintain candidate and active-account views; keep Helio Start activation separate from retained mid-segment and Expansion Assist; report support load per active account, category mix, and account concentration.
- Daniela: own event taxonomy, entitlement and support-state instrumentation, source-of-truth mapping, QA evidence, and backfill evidence; ensure the data path does not infer entitlement from plan name or other proxies; maintain the pending/unresolved QA treatment.
- Ines: keep the two educational lifecycle touches within the conservative, non-state-changing fork; maintain copy and boundary review; do not ship proxy automation or live state-changing branches.
- Customer Success: provide docs-first routine help, own assisted routing for uncertainty and support-heavy cases, and record support category and route so these cases remain visible and separate.
- Riley: perform the final guardrail check on eligibility, unsupported boundaries, lifecycle behavior, cohort separation, and evidence sufficiency before invitations or any scope change.

Each owner is responsible for evidence within this operating shape, not for creating a broader mandate or implying that the beta is a launch program.

6. Language that is not allowed

Do not describe Helio Start as:

- “launched,” “launching,” “GA,” “generally available,” “open,” or “public.”
- A “pricing-page experiment,” “pricing-page plan,” “acquisition motion,” or “paid-growth channel.”
- A “Q4 launch,” “revenue wedge,” “committed with risk,” “forecastable launch,” or Q3 revenue guarantee.
- A broad demand test, representative market read, scalable support proof, or evidence that the admin path is solved.
- A new team charter, permanent operating model, or standing cross-functional program.
- An account “failure,” “rejection,” or “refusal” when the appropriate description is that the request is outside the supported beta path and is being routed to assisted support.
- “Upgrade your plan to unlock team automations” or other plan/entitlement language in a controlled-beta education touch.

Use these terms instead:

- “Capped, invite-only controlled beta.”
- “Selected accounts that meet the documented eligibility gate.”
- “Supported self-serve path” and “assisted route.”
- “Paused pending eligibility or support-boundary review.”
- “Operating-safety and repeatability evidence.”
- “Keep capped versus reconsider later,” with the evidence required for reconsideration stated explicitly.

This vocabulary is part of the operating boundary. It should be used consistently in staff updates, dashboards, lifecycle copy, support notes, and readouts.
