arguments.title: Helio Start capped paid-acquisition proposal — Q2 2026 working draft
arguments.body:
Helio Start capped paid-acquisition proposal — Q2 2026 working draft

Working status and authorization boundary

This is a working proposal for a possible capped Q2 2026 paid-acquisition test. It is not an approval, launch authorization, budget approval, paid-traffic authorization, pipeline target, forecast input, or acquisition claim.

Priya has authorized preparation of this draft. That authorization is limited to preparing the proposal; it does not authorize launch or spend. Any paid test would require separate decisions and approvals, including a separate budget approval. Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026.

Purpose

Translate the two qualifying mature-cohort readouts into a decision-ready, bounded proposal without treating the evidence as causal, scalable acquisition economics, pipeline contribution, or forecast credit. All choices below remain open unless explicitly identified as an existing operating rule or evidence condition.

Evidence basis: two qualifying mature cohorts

The reopening evidence condition is satisfied: two consecutive mature cohorts each had fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes, and neither cohort had an unsupported case enter the admitted path. This satisfies the condition for reopening consideration of a capped proposal; it does not approve the proposal or authorize a paid test.

Cohort 1 — January 27, 2026 certification
- Denominator: 86 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows.
- Mutually exclusive day-90 statuses: 66 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, and 4 on billing hold.
- Gross billed cash: $100,840.
- Refund-adjusted collected cash: $94,760.
- Account-level support effort: 19 minutes median; 84 minutes at p90.
- Support threshold: 4 of 86 accounts, or 4.7%, exceeded 90 support minutes.
- Path integrity: no unsupported case entered the admitted path.

Cohort 2 — February 24, 2026 certification
- Denominator: 91 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows.
- Mutually exclusive day-90 statuses: 71 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, and 4 on billing hold.
- Gross billed cash: $108,230.
- Refund-adjusted collected cash: $102,410.
- Account-level support effort: 18 minutes median; 79 minutes at p90.
- Support threshold: 3 of 91 accounts, or 3.3%, exceeded 90 support minutes.
- Path integrity: no unsupported case entered the admitted path.

Maturity and source limits

- These are complete day-90 windows. Any immature or later window must remain separate and must not be silently folded into the mature read.
- Mature-window status shares are not final long-run retention.
- The exact underlying cohort dates remain missing or unresolved in the certified source record; the certification labels above identify the January 27 and February 24 certification checkpoints, not a reconstructed cohort-start date.
- The two cohorts are descriptive operating evidence. They do not establish causal lift, CAC, payback, scalable acquisition economics, revenue impact, or future-cohort performance.
- Keep statuses mutually exclusive and report day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort together. Do not reduce the evidence gate to a single conversion or cash number.
- The mature-cohort evidence is limited to the admitted-path scope. It does not support conclusions about manual-billing, import, migration, or agency paths that were excluded from the admitted path.

Existing rules and boundaries preserved

The proposal does not change the existing operating rules. The following remain in force:

- Eligibility: retain the approved Helio Start eligibility definition and any required preflight checks; do not broaden eligibility for paid traffic based on the mature-cohort results.
- Refusal: existing refusal conditions and fail-closed handling remain unchanged.
- Connector access: the proposal does not grant, expand, or infer connector access.
- External authority: existing external-authority and ownership requirements remain mandatory. External authority is not blanket permission to contact or message; governed state and applicable messaging rules still control.
- Lifecycle: existing lifecycle states, suppression, renewal/adoption handling, and other lifecycle protections remain unchanged.
- Instrumentation: preserve the existing path-selection, eligibility, admission, and support-routing event taxonomy and required observability. No paid test should begin without instrumentation validation and an accountable source owner.
- Admission: no unsupported case may enter the admitted path. The existing admitted-path definition and refusal handling remain unchanged.
- Support routing: existing support-routing rules, governed handoffs, and escalation paths remain unchanged. Paid traffic does not bypass support triage or create an automatic handoff.
- Organic boundary: Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026. No paid traffic is authorized before that boundary.
- Commercial boundaries: do not assign pipeline, revenue, acquisition, or forecast credit to this evidence or to a future test unless separately approved, defined, measured, and certified.

Open decision 1 — Traffic cap

Decision needed: the maximum paid traffic volume, exposure rate, duration, and any pacing or concentration limits for a possible Q2 test.

Not settled:
- No traffic quantity, percentage, weekly volume, flight length, or pacing schedule is approved.
- No channel mix or allocation is approved.
- No assumption may be made that a capped test will launch once the evidence gate is satisfied.

Required decision record: the accountable approver, exact cap, time basis, audience allocation, pacing method, and conditions for reducing or ending traffic.

Open decision 2 — Budget request

Decision needed: whether to request a budget at all and, if so, the amount, funding source, duration, spend controls, and approval path.

Not settled:
- No dollar amount, test budget, contingency, or spend ceiling is proposed as final.
- No budget is approved or committed.
- Refund-adjusted cohort cash is evidence context, not a funding source, budget justification, or forecast assumption.

Required decision record: requested amount, accounting treatment, approver, spending authority, test period, and confirmation that separate budget approval has been obtained before any launch.

Open decision 3 — Audience and channel

Decision needed: which audience(s) and paid channel(s), if any, could be considered without changing Helio Start eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, admission, or support-routing rules.

Not settled:
- No audience, targeting rule, channel, creative, landing path, or placement is selected.
- No transfer of organic eligibility or external-authority state into paid-contact permission is assumed.
- Any proposed audience mapping, suppression list, source freshness check, and destination must be separately reviewed.

Required decision record: audience definition, exclusion and suppression rules, channel, destination path, consent/contact basis, owner, and rollback mechanism.

Open decision 4 — Success measure

Decision needed: the primary success measure, secondary measures, denominator, maturity window, attribution method, and decision threshold for the proposal or any eventual test.

Not settled:
- No CAC, payback, conversion, retention, paid-active, cash, or support metric is designated as the primary success measure.
- The two mature cohorts do not establish a paid-acquisition benchmark.
- No success measure may convert descriptive organic evidence into causal lift, revenue impact, pipeline contribution, or forecast credit.

Required decision record: predeclared primary metric, supporting metrics, eligible and admitted denominators, complete outcome window, attribution limits, minimum evidence requirements, and decision rule.

Open decision 5 — Support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails

Existing evidence gate to preserve exactly:
- Each of two consecutive mature cohorts must have fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes.
- No unsupported case may enter the admitted path.

Decision needed for any paid test: how these guardrails will be monitored in paid traffic, what denominator and maturity rules apply, whether additional support-capacity limits are required, and who can stop traffic.

Not settled:
- No paid-test support threshold, capacity reserve, contact-rate limit, escalation threshold, or audience-specific guardrail is chosen.
- The mature-cohort evidence does not establish that paid traffic will carry the same support burden.
- Any additional guardrail must supplement, not weaken or replace, the existing two-cohort evidence condition and unsupported-admission prohibition.

Required decision record: support metric definitions, denominator, reporting cadence, capacity owner, escalation route, immediate-stop condition for unsupported admission, and treatment of unresolved classifications.

Open decision 6 — Monitoring and stop rules

Decision needed: monitoring cadence, dashboards and source owners, launch checks, incident process, rollback authority, and predeclared stop or pause rules.

Not settled:

Helio Start capped paid-acquisition proposal — Q2 2026 working draft

Working status and authorization boundary

This is a working proposal for a possible capped Q2 2026 paid-acquisition test. It is not an approval, launch authorization, budget approval, paid-traffic authorization, pipeline target, forecast input, or acquisition claim.

Priya has authorized preparation of this draft. That authorization is limited to preparing the proposal; it does not authorize launch or spend. Any paid test would require separate decisions and approvals, including a separate budget approval. Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026.

Purpose

Translate the two qualifying mature-cohort readouts into a decision-ready, bounded proposal without treating the evidence as causal, scalable acquisition economics, pipeline contribution, forecast credit, or a paid-source result. All choices below remain open unless explicitly identified as an existing operating rule or evidence condition.

Evidence basis: two qualifying mature cohorts

The reopening evidence condition is satisfied: two consecutive mature cohorts each had fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes, and neither cohort had an unsupported case enter the admitted path. This satisfies the condition for reopening consideration of a capped proposal; it does not approve the proposal or authorize a paid test.

Cohort 1 — January 27, 2026 certification
- Denominator: 86 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows.
- Mutually exclusive day-90 statuses: 66 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, and 4 on billing hold.
- Gross billed cash: $100,840.
- Refund-adjusted collected cash: $94,760.
- Account-level support effort: 19 minutes median; 84 minutes at p90.
- Support threshold: 4 of 86 accounts, or 4.7%, exceeded 90 support minutes.
- Path integrity: no unsupported case entered the admitted path.

Cohort 2 — February 24, 2026 certification
- Denominator: 91 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows.
- Mutually exclusive day-90 statuses: 71 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, and 4 on billing hold.
- Gross billed cash: $108,230.
- Refund-adjusted collected cash: $102,410.
- Account-level support effort: 18 minutes median; 79 minutes at p90.
- Support threshold: 3 of 91 accounts, or 3.3%, exceeded 90 support minutes.
- Path integrity: no unsupported case entered the admitted path.

Maturity and source limits

- These are complete day-90 windows. Any immature or later window must remain separate and must not be silently folded into the mature read.
- Mature-window status shares are not final long-run retention.
- The exact underlying cohort dates remain missing or unresolved in the certified source record; the certification labels above identify the January 27 and February 24 certification checkpoints, not a reconstructed cohort-start date. This limitation is unchanged.
- Status remains not board-ready. The evidence condition supports reopening consideration of a bounded proposal, not board readiness, approval, launch authorization, or a paid-acquisition claim.
- The two cohorts are descriptive operating evidence. They do not establish causal lift, CAC, payback, scalable acquisition economics, revenue impact, or future-cohort performance.
- Keep statuses mutually exclusive and report day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort together. Do not reduce the evidence gate to a single conversion or cash number.
- The mature-cohort evidence is limited to the admitted-path scope. It does not support conclusions about manual-billing, import, migration, or agency paths that were excluded from the admitted path.

Existing rules and boundaries preserved

The proposal does not change the existing operating rules. The following remain in force:

- Eligibility: retain the approved Helio Start eligibility definition and any required preflight checks; do not broaden eligibility for paid traffic based on the mature-cohort results.
- Refusal: existing refusal conditions and fail-closed handling remain unchanged.
- Connector access: the proposal does not grant, expand, or infer connector access.
- External authority: existing external-authority and ownership requirements remain mandatory. External authority is not blanket permission to contact or message; governed state and applicable messaging rules still control.
- Lifecycle: use the existing lifecycle branches and current-state suppression behavior. Do not create a paid-source bypass or otherwise bypass lifecycle state, suppression, renewal/adoption handling, or other lifecycle protections.
- Instrumentation: preserve the existing path-selection, eligibility, admission, and support-routing event taxonomy and required observability. For any eventual paid test, paid-source attribution must remain visible from eligibility-flow start through admission, and instrumentation must be validated with an accountable source owner before launch.
- Admission: no unsupported case may enter the admitted path. The existing admitted-path definition and refusal handling remain unchanged.
- Support routing: existing support-routing rules, governed handoffs, and escalation paths remain unchanged. Paid traffic does not bypass support triage or create an automatic handoff.
- Organic boundary: Helio Start remains organic-only through March 31, 2026. No paid traffic is authorized before that boundary.
- Commercial boundaries: do not assign pipeline, revenue, acquisition, or forecast credit to this evidence or to a future test unless separately approved, defined, measured, and certified.

Decision needed: the maximum paid traffic volume, exposure rate, duration, and any pacing or concentration limits for a possible Q2 test.

Not settled:
- No traffic quantity, percentage, weekly volume, flight length, or pacing schedule is approved.
- No channel mix or allocation is approved.
- No assumption may be made that a capped test will launch once the evidence gate is satisfied.

Required decision record: the accountable approver, exact cap, time basis, audience allocation, pacing method, and conditions for reducing or ending traffic.

Open decision 2 — Budget request

Decision needed: whether to request a budget at all and, if so, the amount, funding source, duration, spend controls, and approval path.

Not settled:
- No dollar amount, test budget, contingency, or spend ceiling is proposed as final.
- No budget is approved or committed.
- Refund-adjusted cohort cash is evidence context, not a funding source, budget justification, or forecast assumption.

Required decision record: requested amount, accounting treatment, approver, spending authority, test period, and confirmation that separate budget approval has been obtained before any launch.

- No audience, targeting rule, channel, creative, landing path, or placement is selected.

Required decision record: audience definition, exclusion and suppression rules, channel, destination path, consent/contact basis, owner, and rollback mechanism.

Open decision 4 — Success measure

Decision needed: the primary success measure, secondary measures, denominator, maturity window, attribution method, and decision threshold for the proposal or any eventual test.

Owner inputs incorporated — March 9, 2026:
- Paid-source attribution must remain visible from the start of the eligibility flow through admission. The source must be carried and auditable across those stages; no readout may drop attribution between flow start and admission.

Not settled:
- No CAC, payback, conversion, retention, paid-active, cash, or support metric is designated as the primary success measure.

Open decision 5 — Support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails

Existing evidence gate to preserve exactly:
- Each of two consecutive mature cohorts must have fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes.

Owner inputs incorporated — March 9, 2026:
- Customer Success requires assisted-route reasons and account-level support minutes to be captured from the first contact. This is required monitoring instrumentation, not a post hoc explanation.
- Any unsupported case entering the admitted path remains an immediate stop condition.

Decision needed for any paid test: how these guardrails will be monitored in paid traffic, what denominator and maturity rules apply, whether additional support-capacity limits are required, and who can stop traffic.

Not settled:
- No paid-test support threshold, capacity reserve, contact-rate limit, escalation threshold, or audience-specific guardrail is chosen.
- The mature-cohort evidence does not establish that paid traffic will carry the same support burden.
- Any additional guardrail must supplement, not weaken or replace, the existing two-cohort evidence condition and unsupported-admission prohibition.

Required decision record: support metric definitions, first-contact capture rules, assisted-route reason taxonomy, account-level support-minute calculation, denominator, reporting cadence, capacity owner, escalation route, immediate-stop condition for unsupported admission, and treatment of unresolved classifications.

Open decision 6 — Monitoring and stop rules

Decision needed: monitoring cadence, dashboards and source owners, launch checks, incident process, rollback authority, and predeclared stop or pause rules.

Monitoring inputs incorporated — March 9, 2026:
- From eligibility-flow start through admission, monitor paid-source attribution continuity and reconcile any missing, conflicting, or unclassified source state before relying on the paid readout.
- Monitor day-7 first integration as a leading operating indicator only.
- Track paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort against their complete outcome windows. Do not make a mature claim while any required outcome window is incomplete; keep immature and unresolved classifications visible.
- From first contact, capture assisted-route reasons and account-level support minutes at account level. The monitoring view must retain these fields through reconciliation rather than relying on aggregate or retrospective support summaries.
- Use the existing lifecycle branches and current-state suppression behavior in monitoring and reconciliation. A paid-source label must not create a bypass or override current-state suppression.

Not settled:
- No launch date, monitoring frequency, stop threshold, pause duration, or restart rule is approved.
- No person is yet designated here as the sole rollback authority for a paid test.
- No test should proceed without validated instrumentation, readable operator views, governed state, and a tested rollback path.

Non-negotiable stop or pause conditions to preserve in the decision record:
- Stop immediately if any unsupported case enters the admitted path. This remains an immediate stop condition, not a threshold to be reviewed at the next reporting cadence.
- Stop or pause if required paid-source attribution is missing, broken, conflicting, or not visible from eligibility-flow start through admission, until the state is reconciled and the path is safe.
- Stop or pause if assisted-route reasons or account-level support minutes are not being captured from first contact, or if support effort cannot be reconciled at account level.
- Stop or pause if required eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, admission, or support-routing state cannot be observed or reconciled.
- Do not continue through stale, conflicting, deactivated-admin, or otherwise fail-closed state.
- Do not use a paid-source bypass to circumvent existing lifecycle branches or current-state suppression.

Required decision record: prelaunch checks; live monitors; paid-source continuity checks; day-7 leading-indicator view; complete-window status for paid-active, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort; first-contact support instrumentation; thresholds; alert destinations; incident owner; stop authority; rollback steps; restart criteria; and post-test review owner.

Open decision 7 — Refund-adjusted cash treatment

Evidence treatment to preserve:
- Cohort 1: $100,840 gross billed cash and $94,760 refund-adjusted collected cash.
- Cohort 2: $108,230 gross billed cash and $102,410 refund-adjusted collected cash.
- Gross billed cash must not stand in for cash retained after refunds.
- For any eventual paid readout, refund-adjusted collected cash remains a complete-window outcome measure; day-7 first integration does not replace it.

Decision needed: how refund-adjusted cash should be reported in any proposal or test readout, including the accounting definition, observation window, refund handling, and whether it is descriptive context or a governed test metric.

Not settled:
- Refund-adjusted collected cash is not designated as a success threshold, unit-economics conclusion, revenue forecast, or budget-recovery promise.
- No payback, profitability, revenue, pipeline, or forecast treatment is approved.

Required decision record: metric owner, source of truth, refund window and inclusion rules, reconciliation method, complete outcome-window definition, reporting cadence, and explicit separation from pipeline and forecast treatment.

Open decision 8 — Decision owners

Known status:
- Priya authorized preparation of this working draft. Her authorization does not approve launch or budget.
- The decision owners for traffic cap, budget request, audience/channel, success measure, support guardrails, monitoring/stop rules, and cash treatment remain to be explicitly confirmed.
- Owen supplied the paid-source attribution and outcome-maturity requirements for this proposal; Customer Success supplied the first-contact assisted-route and support-minute requirements; Ines confirmed the existing lifecycle-branch and current-state-suppression treatment. These inputs do not resolve the open decision owners or authorize a launch.

- Tomás Vega retains final board-narrative ownership; this draft does not constitute board approval.

Not settled:
- No placeholder assignment in this section is a final operating decision.
- No decision owner may waive the existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, admission, or support-routing rules.

Revenue, pipeline, and forecast treatment

Exclude pipeline or forecast credit. The two mature cohorts are descriptive evidence for reconsidering a bounded proposal, not evidence of pipeline contribution, forecastable demand, incremental revenue, paid-channel performance, or a commercial commitment. Any future test readout must preserve the same exclusions unless separately approved and certified with its own design, denominator, window, and ownership.

Next decision gate

Before this can become an approved launch plan, the open decisions must be resolved explicitly, source and instrumentation readiness must be verified, the March 31 organic-only boundary must have passed, and separate budget and launch approvals must be recorded. STATUS: APPROVED BOUNDED BATCH — CONDITIONAL START; PAID TRAFFIC OFF

Priya approved one new high-intent Helio Start paid-search batch on October 16, 2027, after reviewing the completed proposal and its certified Q2 2027 mature evidence. This approval is bounded and conditional; it does not mean traffic is live. November 1, 2027 is only the earliest conditional start.

1. Certified Q2 2027 mature evidence reviewed by Priya

- 18 of 25 workspaces were paid-active.
- Refund-adjusted collected cash was $27,860.
- Account-level support effort was 33 minutes at the median and 116 minutes at the 90th percentile.
- Five of 25 workspaces were above 90 support minutes.
- These figures are certified Q2 2027 mature evidence for proposal review. They do not make the approved batch's operating results available for mature claims.
- The approved batch's operating results remain unavailable for mature claims until the fixed cohort has complete day-90 windows. Mature and immature/unresolved windows must remain separate, using the governed status definitions.

2. Approval boundaries

- Approval owner: Priya.
- Exactly one new high-intent Helio Start paid-search batch is approved.
- Spend is capped at $8,000.
- Admissions are capped at 25 workspaces.
- The run closes at the earlier of the $8,000 spend cap or 25 admissions.
- No additional paid batch is authorized.
- There is no pipeline target, no pipeline treatment, and no forecast credit.
- Paid traffic remains off pending Daniela's required launch check; this approval is not a statement that traffic is live.

3. Conditional start and remaining Daniela check

- November 1, 2027 is only the earliest conditional start, not an automatic launch date.
- Before any start, Daniela must confirm the current attribution endpoints, release controls, rollback controls, and the staffed owner-and-backup rota.
- Until that confirmation is complete, keep paid traffic off. No production release or launch is implied by this document.

4. Conditions retained intact

All proposed stop, pause, staffing, attribution, lifecycle, support-clock, eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, instrumentation, and assisted-routing conditions remain intact and binding for any later run. In particular:

- Reconcile paid-source attribution from eligibility-flow start through the final route for every case.
- Preserve existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, hold, suppression, instrumentation, and assisted-routing rules; no paid-source path may bypass them.
- Keep staffing explicit: setup desk as staffed owner, on-duty Customer Success manager as backup, coverage 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Central Monday–Friday, two-business-hour initial-response target, after-hours queueing, and escalation of unclaimed cases to the Customer Success lead.
- Preserve assisted-route reason, transferred handoff context, account-level support minutes from first contact, after-hours handling, and support concentration.
- Treat any attribution reconciliation failure as a pause trigger; retain all proposed stop and pause thresholds, trigger owners, restart authority, and audit treatment.
- Exclude unsupported applicants from the admitted path and verify that no unsupported admission occurred.
- No case may bypass refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, hold, suppression, instrumentation, or assisted-routing controls.

5. Claim and accounting limits

- The batch has no pipeline target, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit.
- Do not make causal, incremental-acquisition, scale, revenue, pipeline, or forecast claims from this bounded batch.
- Do not treat setup-step exposure, first integration, activation, or paid-active status alone as mature commercial evidence.
- Use complete day-90 windows for mature outcome claims; operating results remain unavailable for mature claims until the fixed cohort has complete day-90 windows.
- Report refund-adjusted collected cash and account-level support effort, including both count and share of workspaces exceeding 90 support minutes, with complete windows identified.

6. Decision ownership and authority

- Priya: approval owner for this bounded budget-and-batch decision.
- Daniela: must confirm current attribution endpoints, release and rollback controls, and the staffed owner-and-backup rota before any conditional start; Daniela remains the engineering rollback owner.
- Customer Success/setup desk: staffed coordination owner; on-duty Customer Success manager is backup; Customer Success lead handles escalation of unclaimed cases.
- Riley: preparation and customer-correction/incident-stop owner; no additional batch or launch authority is implied.
- This approval does not create new eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or assisted-routing authority.

Document boundary

This document records Priya's bounded approval for one conditional batch, not live traffic. The sole approved batch is limited to $8,000 and 25 admissions, closing at the earlier cap. No additional paid batch, pipeline target, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, or mature claim from the batch is authorized. Paid traffic must remain off until Daniela completes the required confirmation, and all stated safeguards remain intact.

arguments.body:
STATUS: APPROVED BOUNDED BATCH — PAID INTAKE CLOSED; MATURE EVIDENCE PENDING

This brief records the one approved Helio Start high-intent paid-search batch and its bounded operating transition. The batch is closed to further paid intake. It does not authorize new paid traffic, an additional paid batch, a budget increase, a production change, a pipeline target or treatment, forecast credit, an eligibility change, a lifecycle bypass, a new production consumer, or a launch beyond the separately approved batch.

1. Fixed cohort and certified Q2 2027 evidence

- The fixed admitted cohort for the approved batch is 25 workspaces.
- The certified Q2 2027 evidence reviewed for the approval recorded 18 of 25 workspaces paid-active, $27,860 in refund-adjusted collected cash, 33 minutes of median account-level support effort, 116 minutes at the 90th percentile, and five of 25 workspaces above 90 support minutes.
- Those figures are certified descriptive mature evidence for the prior Q2 evidence set. They do not make the approved batch's operating results mature.
- The approved batch's operating results remain unavailable for mature claims until every admitted workspace has a complete permitted day-90 window.
- Mature, immature, and unresolved windows remain separate and use the governed status definitions. A mature-window share is not automatically final retention.

2. Original approval boundaries retained

- Approval owner: Priya.
- Exactly one high-intent Helio Start paid-search batch was approved.
- Spend was capped at $8,000 and admissions at 25 workspaces; the run closed at the earlier cap.
- No additional paid batch is authorized.
- Paid traffic remains off after the bounded intake has closed; remaining capacity or prior approval does not imply permission to reopen traffic or intake.
- There is no pipeline target, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit.
- Existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, freshness, hold, suppression, instrumentation, dedupe, assisted-routing, correction, incident-stop, and governed-handoff rules remain unchanged.

3. December 14 transition to ordinary account support

Customer Success confirmed, and the transition was accepted on December 14, 2027:

- No new paid intake can arrive.
- All 25 admitted workspaces are assigned to named ordinary account-support owners.
- The existing after-hours support path remains available.
- Account-level support minutes continue from first contact without reset or double counting. The clock does not reset at admission, activation, handoff, route change, or after-hours handling.
- The dedicated paid-intake owner-and-backup rota may end after Friday, December 17.
- Ending the dedicated paid-intake rota does not end ordinary support, after-hours coverage, account-level support-minute capture, evidence records, or the remaining day-90 observation windows.
- Paid traffic remains off, Daniela's controls remain unchanged, and no additional batch is authorized.
- Mature outcome fields remain unavailable until every day-90 window is complete.

This is a staffing and operating transition only. It does not change cohort scope, eligibility, routing, support-clock treatment, evidence definitions, owner authority, correction or incident handling, or claim limits. The staffing-capacity statement and the 25-workspace fixed cohort must not be read as permission for new admissions.

4. Support, service, attribution, and lifecycle safeguards

- Ordinary account support continues under the named owner assignments without displacing or bypassing the ordinary assisted path.
- The existing after-hours path remains available; after-hours handling follows the established service and incident/stop routes.
- Preserve account identity, final route/outcome, timestamps, transferred context, and cumulative support minutes from first contact.
- Reconcile paid-source attribution from eligibility-flow start through the final route for every fixed-cohort case and retain the evidence record through maturity.
- Preserve separate counts and classifications for paid-source flow starts, admissions, assisted routes, ineligible or fail-closed outcomes, held or suppressed outcomes, and attribution failures.
- No case may bypass eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, hold, suppression, instrumentation, assisted-routing, correction, incident-stop, or governed-handoff rules.
- Fail closed on missing, stale, conflicting, deactivated, untrusted, unresolved, or otherwise unsupported governed state.
- Daniela's production attribution, release, cap, audit, monitoring, and rollback controls remain unchanged. The transition does not delegate, weaken, or expand those controls.
- No unsupported applicant may enter the admitted path; any unsupported admission remains an immediate stop condition under the existing process.

5. Claim and accounting limits

- The batch is closed to further paid intake; no new paid-source performance should be inferred after closure.
- Do not make causal, incremental-acquisition, scale, revenue, pipeline, or forecast claims from this descriptive batch.
- Do not treat setup-step exposure, first integration, activation, paid-active status, clean routing, or staffing continuity alone as mature commercial evidence.
- Use complete day-90 windows for mature outcome claims. Immature and unresolved windows cannot be presented as mature results.
- Report refund-adjusted collected cash and account-level support effort with complete windows identified, including both count and share of workspaces exceeding 90 support minutes when the relevant fixed-cohort record is complete.
- A clean control path supports operational integrity observations; it does not establish customer improvement, durable value, mature retention, or institutional effectiveness.
- The effective workaround and any underlying service gap remain separate observations and must not be collapsed into a claim that the institution or service is functioning.
- No remaining evidence window, prior spend authorization, or admissions capacity authorizes reopening intake or starting another batch.

6. Decision ownership and current authority

- Priya: approval owner for the single bounded budget-and-batch decision.
- Daniela: owner of production attribution, release, monitoring, incident handling, cap enforcement, and engineering rollback controls; those controls remain unchanged.
- Customer Success and named ordinary account-support owners: owners of ongoing account support, staffed handoff, after-hours handling, and account-level support evidence.
- Riley: preparation and customer-correction/incident-stop owner within the established boundaries; no additional-batch or traffic-reopening authority is implied.
- The dedicated paid-intake owner-and-backup rota may end after December 17, but ordinary support ownership and evidence ownership continue.
- No owner may waive or alter the existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, admission, support-routing, correction, incident-stop, or claim rules through this transition.

7. Remaining evidence and review state

STATUS: IN PROGRESS — MATURE OUTCOME FIELDS PENDING

- Continue the day-90 observation and classification process for every admitted workspace.
- Keep complete, immature, and unresolved windows mutually distinct.
- Preserve the fixed denominator of 25 admitted workspaces; do not add new admissions or substitute another denominator.
- Continue account-level support-minute capture from first contact without reset or double counting.
- Retain source-to-final-route reconciliation and Daniela's control evidence through the final evidence review.
- Do not issue a mature outcome summary until every day-90 window is complete and the required fields are certified.
- No additional batch, paid traffic reopening, budget expansion, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, or broader claim is authorized by the pending review.

Document boundary

This document records the bounded batch, its closed-to-new-intake transition, and the remaining evidence work. The dedicated paid-intake rota may end after Friday, December 17 without ending ordinary support or any evidence record. Paid traffic remains off; no additional batch is authorized; Daniela's controls remain unchanged; account-level support minutes continue from first contact without reset or double counting; and mature outcome fields remain unavailable until every day-90 window is complete.

input.body:
2026 Helio Start paid-pilot high-support case review

Scope

The review covered all seven mature workspaces that exceeded 90 account-level support minutes in the 2026 paid pilot. This is a case classification and operating read, not evidence of causal acquisition impact or a broader claim about future cohorts.

Case findings

- Five of seven cases (5/7) required coordination for a supported owner-level permission or network-allowlist action after admission. These were external-authority/setup-sequence cases, not ordinary integration troubleshooting. In each case, external-authority status was current and verified yes at admission, and the governed route and lifecycle views agreed.
- Two of seven cases (2/7) required ordinary integration troubleshooting. These were separate from the external owner-permission or network-allowlist coordination cases.

Causes ruled out across all seven

The review found no case involving billing, an unsupported admission, stale state, or conflicting state. It also found no evidence that the external-authority field meaning or the admission decisions were wrong: the relevant authority state was current and verified at admission, and route and lifecycle views were consistent. The identified gap was setup sequence and execution after admission, not eligibility or admission correctness.

Implications for admission and operations

The findings do not support changing eligibility, admission criteria, or fail-closed handling. Admission decisions were correct for these cases, while high support effort exposed a separate onboarding/setup coordination need. The five authority-action cases should therefore be handled operationally rather than by broadening admission.

Follow-up should remain bounded and non-state-changing: offer a connector-specific pre-setup checklist only to admitted workspaces whose selected connector requires an owner-level permission or network-allowlist action, and only when external-authority status is current and verified yes. Missing, stale, conflicting, pending, no, or not-sure authority state should continue through the existing fail-closed or assisted route. Ordinary integration troubleshooting remains a distinct support path. Preserve existing eligibility, admission, assisted-routing, lifecycle, and fail-closed rules; do not infer that the workaround proves the underlying service is functioning or that it will reduce support effort in future cohorts.

__________________________________________________________________

  Approver: __________________________ Date: _____________________
